title: Cross-language SDK error taxonomy, mapping, and streaming ergonomics
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Define and ship a single, language- idiomatic error surface across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs that: 1) standardizes machine-readable error codes and human-friendly actionable messages, 2) documents retryable vs non-retryable behaviors and default retry policies, 3) provides clear streaming ergonomics and backoff semantics, and 4) ensures telemetry (correlation IDs, error tags) is emitted consistently for server and client errors. This ticket focuses on the spec, SDK-level mappings, example usage, test harnesses, and migration guidance for existing customers.
acceptance_criteria: Published error taxonomy doc that maps HTTP/gRPC/Runtime errors to SDK exceptions for Python/TS/Go

SDKs expose stable error classes/types: transient (Retryable), permanent (Fatal), validation (UserInput), auth (AuthError), rate_limit (RateLimitError), streaming-specific (StreamReset/StreamPartialResponse)
All SDKs attach a canonical error.code (string) and optional metadata map/dict with correlation_id, upstream_status, retry_after when applicable
Default retry policy defined in spec and implemented in SDKs with opt-out flag; golden path retries for transient errors only
Streaming APIs provide a clear client-side pattern for partial results + terminal error reporting (example snippets for Python async iterator, TS ReadableStream, Go channel-based iterator)
End-to-end tests that simulate server errors (5xx, 429, connection reset, chunk truncation) and assert SDK behavior and telemetry tags
Migration guide and changelog entry for existing customers describing behaviors that may change
Design reviewed and signed off by Runtime, SDK, Product, and Observability teams

decisions: Use a single canonical error.code string namespace 'redwood.error.<short>' (e.g. redwood.error.rate_limit, redwood.error.model_mismatch)
Expose both machine-readable error.code and human-readable message; message must include one-sentence actionable guidance when possible

Retry semantics: SDKs automatically retry idempotent requests on transient errors with exponential backoff (initial=100ms, factor=2, max_backoff=10s, max_attempts=4). Non-idempotent endpoints are opt-in for retry via explicit parameter
Streaming: differentiate 'partial response + terminal error' vs 'stream reset' with distinct exception types and provide helpers to resume or fail fast
Telemetry: always surface 'correlation_id' from server if present; if missing, SDK must generate a client_correlation_id and include it in logs/metrics
No breaking change to public method signatures; error types may be introduced as new exported classes/types while preserving legacy error message strings for a deprecation period

notes: Compatibility note: older SDK versions may return plain HTTPError strings; new SDKs will add typed exceptions but will still include legacy message for a 3-month deprecation window

Actionable message guidance: keep messages under 180 chars, include suggested user action (eg. 'retry after Xs', 'check API key/permissions', 'reduce prompt length or switch to streaming'), and include a link to docs when appropriate

Testing tip: use network fault injector to simulate TCP resets and truncated chunks; assert that consumer-facing iterator surface either yields partial items with a final StreamPartialResponse error or raises StreamReset depending on server behavior
